section: India - occupational structure: main and marginal workers, work participation rate, cultivators and agricultural labourers
subsections: Cultivators vs agricultural labourers - trend of shift
PLFS indicators - LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate definitions
Female work participation - levels and regional contrast
AP district-wise occupational data - cultivators and agricultural labourers

accepted.s: According to the 2011 Census, which category first exceeded the other in India?
accepted.x: In 2011, agricultural labourers constituted 30.0% of workers, exceeding cultivators at 24.6% for the first time.
accepted.tq: Direct comparison of two closely related occupational categories.
accepted.sec: Cultivators vs agricultural labourers - trend of shift

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the change between 2001 and 2011 in the shares of cultivators and agricultural labourers in India?
o: Cultivators fell from 31.7% to 24.6%, while labourers rose from 26.5% to 30.0%
Cultivators rose from 24.6% to 31.7%, while labourers fell from 30.0% to 26.5%
Cultivators rose from 26.5% to 31.7%, while labourers fell from 31.7% to 30.0%
Cultivators fell from 31.7% to 26.5%, while labourers rose from 24.6% to 30.0%
accepted.x: Cultivators declined from 31.7% in 2001 to 24.6% in 2011, whereas agricultural labourers increased from 26.5% to 30.0%.
accepted.tq: Track the direction of change before comparing the figures.
accepted.sec: Cultivators vs agricultural labourers - trend of shift

accepted.s:
With reference to Andhra Pradesh in 2011, consider the following statements:
1. Agricultural labourers numbered 110.52 lakh.
2. Of the agricultural labourers, 86.12 lakh were main workers and 24.40 lakh were marginal workers.
3. Agricultural labourers constituted about 48% of the workers of Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh had 110.52 lakh agricultural labourers, comprising 86.12 lakh main and 24.40 lakh marginal workers, and they formed about 48% of its workers.
accepted.tq: Verify each numerical component independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Cultivators vs agricultural labourers - trend of shift

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the number of cultivators in 2011 was approximately:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh had 33.40 lakh cultivators in 2011.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total cultivator figure from the separate labourer components.
accepted.sec: Cultivators vs agricultural labourers - trend of shift

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh accounted for approximately what share of India’s main agricultural labourers in 2011?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh accounted for 9.99% of India’s main agricultural labourers.
accepted.tq: Separate a state’s national share from its internal occupational percentage.
accepted.sec: Cultivators vs agricultural labourers - trend of shift

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the gender composition of cultivators and agricultural labourers in 2011?
o: Women constituted 24% of both cultivators and agricultural labourers
Women constituted 55% of agricultural labourers and 24% of cultivators
Women constituted 55% of cultivators and 24% of agricultural labourers
Women constituted 12.8% of agricultural labourers and 55% of cultivators
accepted.x: Women formed 55% of agricultural labourers but only 24% of cultivators. Women held only 12.8% of operational holdings.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the two percentages in a confusable comparison.
accepted.sec: Cultivators vs agricultural labourers - trend of shift

accepted.s: Which factor has contributed to the increasing feminisation of farm work in India?
o: A rise in women’s share of operational holdings to 55%
accepted.x: Men’s out-migration has increased women’s participation in farm work, even though women hold only 12.8% of operational holdings.
accepted.tq: Link the stated demographic movement with its occupational consequence.
accepted.sec: Cultivators vs agricultural labourers - trend of shift

accepted.s: Which statement best reflects the caste-class relationship mentioned in relation to rural occupations?
o: Scheduled Castes are largely employers of agricultural labourers
Scheduled Castes are concentrated exclusively in household industries
Scheduled Castes are mostly large commercial farmers
Scheduled Castes are mostly marginal farmers and landless labourers
accepted.x: Scheduled Castes are described as being concentrated largely among marginal farmers and landless agricultural labourers.
accepted.tq: Use the precise social-group and occupational association rather than an extreme alternative.
accepted.sec: Cultivators vs agricultural labourers - trend of shift

accepted.s: The Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) is defined as:
o: Employed persons as a percentage of the total population
Unemployed persons as a percentage of the labour force
Unemployed persons as a percentage of the total population
Persons in the labour force, employed and unemployed, per 100 persons
accepted.x: LFPR is the proportion of persons in the labour force, comprising both employed and unemployed persons, in the population.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among four closely related labour-market ratios.
accepted.sec: PLFS indicators - LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate definitions

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct expression for the Worker Population Ratio (WPR)?
o: Labour force divided by total population multiplied by 100
Employed persons divided by total population multiplied by 100
Unemployed persons divided by labour force multiplied by 100
Unemployed persons divided by total population multiplied by 100
accepted.x: WPR equals employed persons divided by total population, multiplied by 100.
accepted.tq: Focus on the denominator to distinguish WPR from LFPR and unemployment rate.
accepted.sec: PLFS indicators - LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate definitions

accepted.s: The Unemployment Rate (UR) and Proportion Unemployed (PU) differ because:
o: UR uses total population as denominator, while PU uses labour force
UR uses labour force as denominator, while PU uses total population
Both use employed persons as denominator
Both use total population as denominator
accepted.x: UR is unemployed persons as a percentage of the labour force, whereas PU is unemployed persons as a percentage of the total population.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the denominator of each indicator.
accepted.sec: PLFS indicators - LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate definitions

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding PLFS status approaches:
1. Usual status uses a 365-day reference period.
2. Under UPSS, a person is counted as employed if the person worked for at least 30 days in the year.
3. CWS requires at least one hour of work on any one day of the reference week.
4. CDS records the activity status for each day of the week.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the reference periods and employment criteria of usual status, UPSS, CWS and CDS.
accepted.tq: Check each method against its reference period and minimum work criterion.
accepted.sec: PLFS indicators - LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate definitions

accepted.s: A person worked for one hour on one day during a seven-day week. Under which PLFS approach would this criterion be relevant?
accepted.x: Current Weekly Status counts work of at least one hour on any one day of the seven-day reference week.
accepted.tq: Match the duration of the reference period with the status approach.
accepted.sec: PLFS indicators - LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate definitions

accepted.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey is conducted by the:
o: NITI Aayog under the Ministry of Finance
Registrar General of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs
Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Rural Development
accepted.x: The PLFS is conducted by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
accepted.tq: Use the institution-authority association to reject swapped departmental options.
accepted.sec: PLFS indicators - LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate definitions

accepted.s: Headline PLFS rates generally refer to which age group?
accepted.x: Headline PLFS rates are generally reported for persons aged 15 years and above, unless the question specifies another age range.
accepted.tq: Read the age qualifier carefully before interpreting a labour indicator.
accepted.sec: PLFS indicators - LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate definitions

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly gives the annual PLFS 2025 values for LFPR, WPR and UR, respectively?
accepted.x: The annual PLFS 2025 figures were 59% for LFPR, 57% for WPR and approximately 3% for unemployment rate.
accepted.tq: Preserve the order of the three indicators while matching the annual release figures.
accepted.sec: PLFS indicators - LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate definitions

accepted.s: For January–March 2026 under CWS for persons aged 15 years and above, which combination is correct?
accepted.x: For January–March 2026, the CWS estimates were LFPR 55.5%, WPR 52.8% and UR 5.0%.
accepted.tq: Match the release period and survey status before comparing the figures.
accepted.sec: PLFS indicators - LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate definitions

accepted.s: In January–March 2026, the urban and rural unemployment rates under CWS were, respectively:
accepted.x: The unemployment rate was 6.6% in urban areas and 4.3% in rural areas during January–March 2026.
accepted.tq: Watch the order of urban and rural figures in a regional comparison.
accepted.sec: PLFS indicators - LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate definitions

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about unemployment among educated persons is correct?
o: Secondary-and-above educated unemployment was 7.2%, with rural unemployment higher than urban unemployment.
Educated unemployment was 3%, uniformly in rural and urban areas.
Secondary-and-above educated unemployment was 6.5%, with urban unemployment at 7.2% and rural unemployment at 6%.
Urban educated unemployment was 4.5%, while rural educated unemployment was 5%.
accepted.x: Unemployment among persons educated to secondary level and above was 6.5%; it was 7.2% in urban areas and 6% in rural areas.
accepted.tq: Compare the overall, urban and rural values without reversing the regional order.
accepted.sec: PLFS indicators - LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate definitions

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Andhra Pradesh PLFS 2023–24 estimates under usual status for all ages?
o: LFPR 59.5% and WPR 57.0% for the whole population
LFPR 35.8% and WPR 34.5% for the whole population
LFPR 47.5% and WPR 45.6%, both above the corresponding Indian figures of 45.1% and 43.7%
LFPR 45.1% and WPR 43.7%, both above the corresponding Andhra Pradesh figures
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded an LFPR of 47.5% and WPR of 45.6%, compared with India’s 45.1% and 43.7%, respectively.
accepted.tq: Compare state and national values while retaining the correct indicator order.
accepted.sec: PLFS indicators - LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate definitions

accepted.s: Which pair correctly represents the male and female LFPR in Andhra Pradesh in 2023–24?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh’s LFPR was 59.5% for males and 35.8% for females in 2023–24.
accepted.tq: Distinguish LFPR from WPR before matching the gender figures.
accepted.sec: PLFS indicators - LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate definitions

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the rise in India’s female LFPR for persons aged 15 years and above?
accepted.x: Female LFPR rose from 23.3% in 2017–18 to 30% in 2019–20, 37% in 2022–23 and about 40% in 2025.
accepted.tq: Arrange the dated values in chronological order and check the upward trend.
accepted.sec: Female work participation - levels and regional contrast

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly gives the rural and urban female LFPR in 2022–23?
accepted.x: In 2022–23, female LFPR was 41.5% in rural areas and 25.4% in urban areas.
accepted.tq: Use the rural–urban contrast to identify the correctly paired figures.
accepted.sec: Female work participation - levels and regional contrast

accepted.s: Between 2019–20 and 2025, rural female LFPR rose from 33.0% to 45.9%, whereas urban female LFPR rose from:
accepted.x: Urban female LFPR increased from 23.3% in 2019–20 to 27.7% in 2025, much less than the rural increase.
accepted.tq: Compare the size of rural and urban changes rather than only their ending values.
accepted.sec: Female work participation - levels and regional contrast

accepted.s: What share of the rise in female workers between 2017–18 and 2023–24 was contributed by rural women?
accepted.x: Rural women contributed 80% of the rise in female workers between 2017–18 and 2023–24.
accepted.tq: Identify the contribution share, not the female LFPR level.
accepted.sec: Female work participation - levels and regional contrast

accepted.s: Which set of states led the rural gains in female work participation?
o: West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Tamil Nadu
accepted.x: West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar led the rural gains in female work participation.
accepted.tq: Match the regional trend with the stated leading states.
accepted.sec: Female work participation - levels and regional contrast

accepted.s: The U-shaped curve of female work participation is associated with the work of:
accepted.x: The U-shaped relationship in female work participation is associated with Claudia Goldin.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the named economist and other prominent economists.
accepted.sec: Female work participation - levels and regional contrast

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a reason for the rise in female work participation?
o: Subsistence farming and unpaid family work
Distress after the 2017 slowdown and COVID-related return migration
Universal availability of flexible working hours
accepted.x: Universal availability of flexible working hours was not identified as a reason for the rise. The stated reasons include subsistence farming, unpaid family work, economic distress, return migration and broader survey coverage.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses a stated condition rather than describing it.
accepted.sec: Female work participation - levels and regional contrast

accepted.s: Which of the following factors has contributed to low female work participation in India?
o: Mechanisation reducing manual demand, increased female education and lack of flexible hours
Only the expansion of subsistence farming
Decline in girls’ education and complete workplace safety
accepted.x: Mechanisation, greater participation of girls in education, lack of flexible hours, workplace distance, safety concerns and family duties have contributed to low female work participation.
accepted.tq: Select the comprehensive option while rejecting extreme or reversed causes.
accepted.sec: Female work participation - levels and regional contrast

accepted.s: India followed the first half of Claudia Goldin’s U-curve in female work participation up to:
accepted.x: India followed the first half of the U-curve in female work participation up to 2018–19.
accepted.tq: Match the stated turning-period boundary with the correct year.
accepted.sec: Female work participation - levels and regional contrast

accepted.s: Which statement correctly compares female work participation in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Female WPR was 39.6% in rural areas and 22.8% in urban areas; urban young women aged 15–29 had a WPR of only 15.9%.
Female WPR was 45.9% in rural areas and 27.7% in urban areas; young women had a WPR of 41.7%.
Female WPR was 22.8% in rural areas and 39.6% in urban areas; urban young women had a WPR of 35.8%.
Female WPR was 35.8% in rural areas and 31.7% in urban areas; young women had a WPR of 23.3%.
accepted.x: In Andhra Pradesh, female WPR was 39.6% in rural areas and 22.8% in urban areas. Among urban women aged 15–29, it was only 15.9%.
accepted.tq: Check both the rural–urban comparison and the age-specific urban figure.
accepted.sec: Female work participation - levels and regional contrast

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes non-workers in India in 2011?
o: They numbered 7,288.27 lakh and constituted about 60% of the population
They numbered 3,340 lakh and constituted about 24.6% of the population
They numbered 1,100.52 lakh and constituted about 48% of the population
They numbered 86.12 lakh and constituted about 30% of the population
accepted.x: There were 7,288.27 lakh non-workers in 2011, amounting to about 60% of the population.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the non-worker total from occupational subgroup figures.
accepted.sec: Non-workers categories and dependency

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a Census category of non-workers?
accepted.x: The Census categories include students, household-duty persons, dependants, pensioners, rentiers, beggars or vagrants and others. Permanent industrial employers are not listed as a category.
accepted.tq: Identify the outsider in a classification list.
accepted.sec: Non-workers categories and dependency

accepted.s: Which demographic change indicates a rise in the working-age share and a fall in the child share?
o: Working-age population fell to 24%, while children rose to 66.4%
Working-age population remained at 45.1%, while children fell to 31.7%
Working-age population rose to 66.4%, while children aged 0–14 fell to 24%
Both working-age and child populations rose to 66.4%
accepted.x: The working-age group aged 15–59 rose to 66.4% of the population, while the 0–14 age group declined to 24%.
accepted.tq: Match each age group with its correct share and direction of change.
accepted.sec: Non-workers categories and dependency

accepted.s: Which district had the highest share of agricultural labourers among total workers in Andhra Pradesh in 2011?
accepted.x: West Godavari had the highest share of agricultural labourers among total workers in 2011, associated with its delta paddy economy.
accepted.tq: Use the district–occupation association and avoid swapping the two rankings.
accepted.sec: AP district-wise occupational data - cultivators and agricultural labourers  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
